# tritonctl route-table

Manage route tables

Subcommands: list, show, create, delete

Usage: `tritonctl route-table [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

## tritonctl route-table list

List route tables in the project, or on one VPC

Alias: ls

Usage: `tritonctl route-table list [OPTIONS]`

- `--vpc <VPC>`: Only the tables of this VPC (name, uuid, or prefix)

## tritonctl route-table show

Show one route table

Usage: `tritonctl route-table show [OPTIONS] <ID>`

- `<ID>`: Table name, uuid, or prefix

## tritonctl route-table create

Create a route table inside a VPC. Every VPC has a main table already; this adds another

Usage: `tritonctl route-table create [OPTIONS] --vpc <VPC> --name <NAME>`

- `--vpc <VPC>`: VPC to create it in (name, uuid, or prefix) (required)
- `--name <NAME>` (required)
- `--description <DESCRIPTION>`

## tritonctl route-table delete

Delete a route table

Alias: rm

Usage: `tritonctl route-table delete [OPTIONS] <ID>`

- `<ID>`: Table name, uuid, or prefix
- `-n, --dry-run`: Print what would change and stop
- `-y, --yes`: Answer yes to the confirmation. The summary still prints
- `--keep-going`: Keep executing after a step fails
